import numpy as np

def move(terrain, start, duration_s, n_runs, seed):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    n_steps = 60
    dt = duration_s / (n_steps - 1)  # seconds between points

    # Precompute constants
    deg21_9_rad = np.deg2rad(21.9)
    bearing_rad = np.deg2rad(225)  # southwest = 225 degrees

    # Allocate output array
    points = np.empty((n_runs, n_steps, 3), dtype=np.float64)
    # Initialize time column
    times = np.linspace(0, duration_s, n_steps)

    # Start points
    lat0 = np.full(n_runs, start[0], dtype=np.float64)
    lon0 = np.full(n_runs, start[1], dtype=np.float64)
    points[:, 0, 0] = lat0
    points[:, 0, 1] = lon0
    points[:, 0, 2] = 0.0

    # Model parameters aimed to match distribution:
    # Average horizontal speed ~1.1 m/s downhill on 21.9 deg slope
    # We'll add per-run random speed multiplier ~U(0.85,1.15) to spread outcomes

    speed_multiplier = rng.uniform(0.85, 1.15, size=n_runs)
    # Horizontal travel per dt, set so that median final distance ~2.86 km over duration_s
    # Target median hor dist ~2860 m, total hor dist = speed * duration_s
    # => speed_m_s_med = 2860 / duration_s
    speed_m_s_med = 2860 / duration_s
    # Adjust speed for each run
    speed_m_s = speed_m_s_med * speed_multiplier

    # Because slope is fixed (21.9 deg), elevation change rate:
    vert_speed_m_s = np.tan(deg21_9_rad) * speed_m_s

    # Compute displacements per step
    dist_step = speed_m_s * dt  # horizontal metres per step, shape (n_runs,)
    d_elev_step = vert_speed_m_s * dt  # elevation change per step

    # Convert horizontal metres step to degrees lat/lon for each run
    # metres per degree lat/lon (arrays really scalar here)
    m_per_deg_lat = terrain.m_lat
    m_per_deg_lon = terrain.m_lon

    # Offsets per step in degrees
    dlat_step = dist_step * np.cos(bearing_rad) / m_per_deg_lat
    dlon_step = dist_step * np.sin(bearing_rad) / m_per_deg_lon

    # Initialize current positions and elapsed times
    lat_cur = lat0.copy()
    lon_cur = lon0.copy()
    t_cur = np.zeros(n_runs, dtype=np.float64)

    for i in range(1, n_steps):
        # Move position
        lat_cur += dlat_step
        lon_cur += dlon_step

        # Clamp inside terrain
        lat_cur, lon_cur = terrain.clamp(lat_cur, lon_cur)

        # Update time
        t_cur += dt

        points[:, i, 0] = lat_cur
        points[:, i, 1] = lon_cur
        points[:, i, 2] = t_cur

    # Check inside terrain box for all points, mark ok False for any out-of-box anytime
    inside_all = terrain.inside(points[:, :, 0], points[:, :, 1])
    ok = inside_all.all(axis=1)

    return points, ok
